title: Upbit trading volume spikes 273% as South Korean investors re-enter crypto
summary: One analyst said South Korean capital is slowly moving back to crypto, as investors are 'return-chasing' rather than 'asset-loyal.'
content:
Daily trading volume on South Korea’s leading cryptocurrency exchange Upbit surged by 273% as retail investors aggressively returned to digital asset markets.
The sharp liquidity influx was largely driven by a wave of new token listings alongside a broader global market rally.
Data shows local traders are rapidly shifting back into speculative altcoin pairs, aiming to capture short-term momentum and outsized returns.
The sudden spike in trading activity pushed South Korea’s "Kimchi Premium" higher, reflecting strong domestic buying pressure relative to global price averages.
The volume surge solidifies Upbit’s market dominance in the region, reaffirming South Korea as one of the world's most active retail crypto hubs.

title: Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins key approval to offer crypto services in Japan
summary:
Japan's crypto market maturity accelerates, attracting institutional interest and necessitating robust infrastructure and trusted services.
The post Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins key approval to offer crypto services in Japan appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Laser Digital, the digital-asset subsidiary of Nomura Holdings, has officially completed its registration as a crypto asset exchange operator in Japan.
The regulatory clearance from the Kanto Local Finance Bureau permits the firm to offer institutional trading and asset brokerage services.
The expansion aims to tap into growing domestic demand as Japanese institutional interest in digital asset allocation reaches record levels.
Alongside trading, Laser Digital is partnering with local entities to explore Japanese yen and U.S. dollar stablecoin issuance.
The milestone reinforces Nomura’s strategy to build a globally regulated crypto infrastructure across Asia, Europe, and the U.S.

South Korean lawmakers seek expanded FIU powers over unregistered crypto firms
summary: The proposal would let the FIU investigate suspected violations and refer unregistered crypto operators directly to law enforcement.
content:
South Korean lawmakers have introduced a bill to grant the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) direct authority to investigate unregistered crypto firms.
The proposed amendment allows the agency to independently analyze suspected violations and refer cases directly to law enforcement.
Under the new framework, any citizen would be able to report suspected illegal or unregistered virtual asset operators to the FIU.
Lawmakers cited enforcement gaps under current laws, where police stalled investigations into most FIU-referred unregistered firms.
The measure aims to strengthen anti-money laundering controls and crack down on offshore entities targeting local retail investors.

title: US plans unprecedented sanctions on Iran, escalating tensions: Bessent
summary:
The sanctions could further destabilize regional relations and diminish prospects for future diplomatic agreements between the U.S. and Iran.
The post US plans unprecedented sanctions on Iran, escalating tensions: Bessent appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that Washington is preparing to implement the "toughest sanctions in history" against Iran as part of an aggressive "maximum economic pressure" campaign.  Coordinated Economic Isolation: The strategy aims to completely sever Tehran's remaining commercial ties, with secondary sanctions targeting any country or firm that continues to trade with Iran.  Strait of Hormuz Enforcement: The financial measures will run parallel to an ongoing maritime blockade restricting commercial vessel transit and port access.  Explicit Policy Objectives: Administration officials have framed the unprecedented financial squeeze as a non-kinetic mechanism designed to force a resolution to the ongoing conflict.  The announcement has added further volatility to global energy markets, driving Brent crude prices above $92 per barrel amid escalating supply disruption fears. Treasury officials are expected to outline the specific details of the sanctions package

title: Aston Villa faces squad challenges after selling three key players
summary:
Aston Villa's squad depth and cohesion face challenges, risking inconsistency in multiple competitions despite financial gains from sales.
The post Aston Villa faces squad challenges after selling three key players appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Aston Villa is navigating an unprecedented squad rebuild as financial sustainability demands and high-profile transfers reshape their roster ahead of the new season.
The club has sanctioned major departures, including core midfielders Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers, alongside defender Lucas Digne and centre-back Ezri Konsa.
Compounding the roster overhaul, an early-season injury wave has sidelined key players Amadou Onana and summer recruit João Gomes.
Manager Unai Emery has brought in replacements such as Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and prospect Brian Madjo to patch critical depth gaps.
With additional star figures like Ollie Watkins continuing to attract heavy international transfer interest, Villa's remaining squad depth faces an immediate test.
Navigating this rapid transition smoothly will determine whether the club can maintain its top-four competitiveness or suffer an extended period of adjustment.

title: CZ Wants Countries to Tokenize Assets, But There’s A Catch
summary:
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said tokenization could help countries raise money and attract foreign investment, while acknowledging that putting assets on multiple blockchains could fragment liquidity.  His comments come as the tokenization market continues to expand, with the total value of distributed assets now at $38.40 billion. CZ Pushes For Global Tokenization  Zhao framed
The post CZ Wants Countries to Tokenize Assets, But There’s A Catch appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content:
Former Binance CEO Changpeng "CZ" Zhao urged governments to tokenize state assets, stock markets, and issue sovereign stablecoins to attract foreign direct investment.
According to updates shared on Binance Square, CZ has been meeting with government officials and regulators across Asia to accelerate real-world asset (RWA) adoption.
However, CZ highlighted a major catch: deploying assets across multiple blockchains creates significant fragmented liquidity.
He emphasized that overcoming this obstacle requires high asset interchangeability and standardized frameworks among different token issuers.
Analysis covered by Mitrade indicates that sovereign RWA initiatives could unlock hundreds of billions in market value as governments look to expand global capital access.

title: OpenAI IPO pause raises questions about Anthropic’s public offering plans
summary:
OpenAI's IPO pause may signal broader market or regulatory challenges, potentially affecting Anthropic's valuation and strategic decisions.
The post OpenAI IPO pause raises questions about Anthropic’s public offering plans appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar reassured staff that the firm is targeting a public debut by 2027, dismissing IPO race pressure as rival Anthropic prepares to go public.
The update follows OpenAI's confidential IPO filing in June alongside a temporary pause on certain training workloads to overhaul internal safety protocols.
Meanwhile, Anthropic has submitted its own confidential paperwork and could list as early as September 2026, backed by annualized revenue approaching $65 billion.
Management urged employees not to worry if Anthropic debuts first, emphasizing that OpenAI is operating on its own independent timeline.
Market analysts believe Anthropic’s public prospectus will provide the first true audited look at revenue trajectories and compute costs across the AI industry
